rules.title: New Jersey Anti-Eviction Act – good cause required to evict or refuse to renew
rules.requirement: A residential landlord may not evict a tenant or fail to renew a lease (written or oral) without good cause, and must prove in court that statutory grounds exist. Possession may be recovered only by consent or through court eviction process; each cause other than nonpayment must be described in a written notice, and a Notice to Quit is required for all good-cause evictions except nonpayment.
rules.coverage_text: Most residential rental properties, including single-family homes, mobile homes and land in mobile home parks, apartment buildings and complexes, and rooming and boarding homes.

exemption_tests.description: May not apply to two- or three-unit owner-occupied premises with two or fewer rental units.

Does not apply to hotel guests, motel guests, or guest houses rented to a transient guest or seasonal tenant (hotel/motel occupants with no alternate residence who live there continually are covered).
Does not apply to a unit held in trust on behalf of an immediate family member who is developmentally disabled and permanently occupies the unit.

rules.exemptions_text: May not apply to two- or three-unit owner-occupied premises with two (2) or fewer rental units; hotel/motel/guest house transient or seasonal guests; units held in trust for a developmentally disabled immediate family member who permanently occupies the unit.
rules.key_value: Good cause required; statutory grounds include nonpayment, disorderly conduct, property damage, breach of rules or lease covenants, failure to pay a rent increase, and health/safety or removal from rental market.
rules.quoted_span:
No residential landlord may evict or fail to renew a 
lease, whether it is a written or an oral lease without good cause.
rules.ambiguity_note: Exemption text is internally unclear ("two- or three-unit owner-occupied premises with two (2) or fewer rental units"). Source is a state agency summary publication.
